title: EXP-047-R2 — Hello World Part 2: Derived FX_UM Property Class Creation and Recovery (replay after session expiry)
objective: Using only the supported Mongoose Web Client Property Classes runtime Form (IdoPropertyClasses), establish that the derived property class FX_UM does not already exist, then create exactly one FX_UM property class with Base Class FX_UMBase, Domain IDO FX_UMs, Domain Property FX_UM, and Additional List Properties FX_Description. Preserve the inherited data type, length, and Label String ID FX_sUM without manually overriding them. Record which property fields visibly display override asterisks. Perform exactly one ordinary toolbar Save, verify the clean post-Save state, close and reopen the Property Classes runtime Form through native navigation, execute one fresh exact-name collection query, and verify recovery of the four configured relationships and the observable inherited properties. Preserve FX_UMBase and all other existing artifacts unchanged. The experiment establishes same-session runtime UI-level metadata recovery only.

in_scope: Read the EXP-043, EXP-044, EXP-045 and EXP-046 records for established object identity, baseline metadata and supported navigation procedures.

Replay of EXP-047, which was blocked in T1 by a Web Client "Session Expired" alert before the FX_UMBase positive control; nothing was created. The operator has answered that alert, signed in again and loaded the Web Client. Expect earlier runtime tabs to be gone. If a Property Classes tab with an unsaved placeholder row is still open, do not type into or save it; record it, and a native Close of that clean placeholder-only Form (no Save) is allowed once. Any Save/discard prompt on that close is a stop. If a sign-in or Session Expired screen appears, stop.
Verify the existing authenticated Mongoose Web Client session, configuration, Property Classes runtime Form identity and clean state before mutation.
Use the vendor IdoPropertyClasses runtime Form solely as the supported interface for inspecting and creating the FX_UM metadata record; do not edit the Form definition.
Read FX_UMBase as a positive-control property class and baseline its Class Name, Data Type, Length, Label String ID and existing operator checkout state wherever the supported UI exposes them.

Establish the absence of FX_UM through one fresh native Filter-in-Place class-name query (exact text FX_UM) with a working FX_UMBase positive control. Stop before creation if a FX_UM class exists or the result is ambiguous. A result listing only other classes (for example FX_UMBase, if the filter matches by prefix) counts as zero FX_UM matches; record which matching rule was observed. Case-insensitive coverage is accepted by inference from the case-insensitive Mongoose filters observed in EXP-040 and EXP-044 (operator decision, EXP-044); do not type lowercase or other case variants (the exact-value guard denies them by design).
Create exactly one FX_UM property class through the native New action.
Set Base Class to exactly FX_UMBase.
Set Domain IDO to exactly FX_UMs.
Set Domain Property to exactly FX_UM.
Set Additional List Properties to exactly FX_Description.
Observe inherited Data Type, Length and Label String ID FX_sUM where exposed by the native UI, without explicitly editing these values.
Capture the visible override-asterisk state of the four configured fields and any inherited fields exposed by the UI, without assuming which fields must display an asterisk.
Verify all four configured values in the new record before invoking Save.
Invoke exactly one ordinary Property Classes runtime toolbar Save and capture its immediate settled result, messages, row indicators and Save state.
Close the clean Property Classes runtime Form exactly once and reopen it exactly once using supported Web Client navigation.
Execute one fresh native exact-name query for FX_UM after reopening, and inspect the recovered record.
Compare the recovered metadata with the pre-Save values and compare FX_UMBase with its read-only baseline.
Capture screenshots, accessibility snapshots and concise evidence summaries under evidence/EXP-047-R2/.
Create or modify only the EXP-047-R2 experiment record and evidence files in the repository.
Classify any successful result as observed, not replay_verified.
out_of_scope: Creating or modifying any property class other than the new FX_UM record.
Changing FX_UMBase or its existing operator checkout state.
Changing the FX_UMs IDO, its FX_UM or FX_Description property definitions, or applying FX_UM as a property class to either property.
Changing dbo.FX_UMs, including the existing EA / Each and DZ / Dozen records.
Creating or modifying SQL tables, IDO projects, Forms, components, string resources or other metadata definitions.
Editing the vendor IdoPropertyClasses Form in Web Designer.
Changing the inherited Data Type, Length or Label String ID manually.
Creating event handlers, scripts, validation rules or additional domain relationships.
Any manual metadata checkout or check-in, including for the newly created FX_UM.
Metadata synchronization, explicit cache unloading, FormSync, deployment and configuration changes.
Testing runtime property-class application or behavior in FX_UMs.
Independent database durability, cross-session persistence or replay verification.

prohibited_actions: Creating, modifying or deleting any non-FX_ artifact
Starting any other experiment or replay
Modifying production data or disabling security
Reading or printing credential values
Do not create or change any non-FX_ artifact.
Do not change FX_UMBase or its existing checkout state.
Do not edit the FX_UMs IDO or either of its properties.
Do not alter the EA / Each or DZ / Dozen application records.
Do not create FX_UM if any existing exact or case-insensitive class-name match is found, or if the collision gate is ambiguous.
Do not create more than one property-class record.
Do not change any fields other than Class Name, Base Class, Domain IDO, Domain Property and Additional List Properties for the new record.
Do not explicitly set inherited Data Type, Length or Label String ID.
Do not perform more than one explicit toolbar Save, or retry an ambiguous Save.
Do not manually check in or check out FX_UM or FX_UMBase.
If creating, saving or using FX_UM requires a metadata checkout, deployment, unload or additional configuration step, stop and record the prerequisite instead of performing it.
Do not enter data or proceed after an unexpected implicit commit, validation error, Save or discard prompt, timeout, authentication challenge or unexplained state.
Do not repair, delete, overwrite or rename an existing property-class record.
Do not use Web Designer to modify the Property Classes Form.
Do not use direct SQL, internal APIs, browser-executed JavaScript or unsupported writing mechanisms.
Do not restart services, refresh the browser, or establish a replacement session to bypass a failed prerequisite.
Limit browser recovery to one fresh untargeted snapshot and one corrected visible inspection, then stop and record the blocker.
Do not infer metadata persistence solely from the immediate post-Save UI.
Do not claim database-level durability or replay verification from this single execution.
Do not start another experiment or change repository files outside EXP-047.

acceptance_checks.description: Preflight: evidence/EXP-047-R2/ shows an authenticated, usable Web Client, the native Property Classes runtime Form identified as IdoPropertyClasses, no unexpected prompt, Save disabled and no pending unrelated changes. Record the current configuration and editing context. The vendor Form definition remains untouched.

Target absence: a fresh supported native class-name query, with no retained restrictive criteria, returns zero existing exact or case-insensitive matches for FX_UM. A known-existing FX_UMBase positive-control query returns its expected row, demonstrating that the filter and collection retrieval work. Capture the criteria state, filtered result, identity and count evidence. If the absence cannot be established reliably, creation is prohibited.

Base-class baseline: read-only evidence identifies the existing FX_UMBase property class and its available Data Type, Length and Label String ID fields, including FX_sUM where visibly established. Record its current checkout indication without changing it. No new class has been created at this stage.

Derived-class configuration: before Save, exactly one new FX_UM row visibly identifies Class Name FX_UM, Base Class FX_UMBase, Domain IDO FX_UMs, Domain Property FX_UM and Additional List Properties FX_Description. The worker confirms these values in native field controls or captured accessibility properties and reports any screenshot clipping. No second class or unrelated field modification is observed.

Inheritance and override indicators: the new FX_UM record is inspected before Save. Capture the observable effective Data Type, Length and Label String ID where the runtime exposes them, and explicitly inventory the fields showing override asterisks. Confirm no manual changes were made to inherited values. If inherited values or override indicators are not exposed, record that limitation without inventing values or asterisk states.

Single Save: exactly one ordinary toolbar Save is invoked after verifying the new class definition. Evidence captures the Save action and settled result, including FX_UM identity, Save state, row indicators and any message. No validation error, unexpected prompt or ambiguous commit result remains. No additional Save or metadata lifecycle action occurs.

Runtime lifecycle: after Save reaches a demonstrably clean state, the Property Classes Form closes once through its native Form-tab control without an unexpected Save or discard prompt. It then reopens once through supported Web Client navigation. Capture the closed state and reopened Form identity before running the recovery query.

Recovery: one fresh native exact-name query after reopening retrieves exactly one FX_UM class record. Its Base Class is FX_UMBase, Domain IDO is FX_UMs, Domain Property is FX_UM and Additional List Properties is FX_Description. Compare recovered inherited values and override-asterisk states wherever the native UI exposes them. Save is disabled and no unsaved-change indication or unexpected message appears. Capture the queried result and field details, with evidence limitations stated.

Preservation: read-only comparison establishes that FX_UMBase still presents its original baseline properties and operator checkout indication. The worker records that no supported mutation of FX_UMBase, the FX_UMs IDO, its data, strings, Forms or other existing objects occurred. Any aspect that cannot be independently verified must be qualified rather than claimed as proven.

Final audit: reconcile the absence gate, one class creation, one New, one Save, one Form close, one Form reopen and one recovery query against screenshots and controller action records. Inventory the single FX_UM artifact, confirm repository changes are confined to the EXP-047-R2 record and evidence directory, and distinguish observed runtime metadata recovery from untested database durability, cross-session persistence and application of the property class to an IDO property. Classify the finding as observed only.

initial_instruction: T1 — READ-ONLY PREFLIGHT AND CREATION GATE; NO CREATION. Replay of EXP-047 (blocked by session expiry; read its operator outcome block). Create the EXP-047-R2 record and evidence directory. Take a fresh snapshot of each open tab; confirm the authenticated Web Client and DEM configuration. Open the Property Classes runtime Form through Select Form (key-event filter) if it is not open. Capture the FX_UMBase read-only baseline (Data Type, Length, Column Data Type, Label String ID, checkout indication). Then run the creation gate with one fresh Filter-in-Place query for FX_UM (exact text) and one for the positive control FX_UMBase, capturing the criteria before F4 and the settled result after each. Record the matching rule observed. Do not invoke New, type into a placeholder row, Save, check in or check out anything, or open the Designer. Report whether the gate is established, the evidence paths and the final browser state.
